items.title: Lou Donaldson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: What happened, one night in the Paradise I was there, and he came in, and I was sitting in with Big Nick Nicholas

ctx.x: Did you ever sit in with him?

Mmm-hmm. What happened, one night in the Paradise I was there, and he came in, and I was sitting in with Big Nick Nicholas, and when Charlie Parker came in, there were about ten saxophone players on the stand, and all of them ran, you know, like a rattlesnake was coming in there. I was getting ready to get off the stand, too, and he said, “No, you play with me.” I said, “Man, I’m not playing with you.” He said, “Yeah. If you don’t play, I’m not going to play.” So the manager comes by and says, “Man, you’ve got to…
You mean, he’d invented it, but he hadn’t memorized it.

items.title: 67619_Big Nick Nicholas oral history interview
items.q: if he's young like Lou Donaldson

ctx.x: This was it! (laughter) And then I decided that Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday would be for the guys, you know, when they come in I'd announce their names and make 'em feel comfortable, no matter what style they played, and if there was new-comers comin' up, I'd announce their names and if he's young like Lou Donaldson and Horace Silvers (sic), like Horace Silvers worked there with me for a while and, you know, Monk and everybody, like Bird was there all the time and Bill Holiday, she would come in with…
Yeah, this particular thing, but there's a number of questions I still have about the Paradise. Who owned the place and who managed it and what was that all about?
